answer: Falcon-timing admission: identities must sustain a burst shape—request gaps with variance held inside a signed band—before gaining write access. Each opal-tier agent runs a local clock attestation, so sustained rate is judged per early minute, not totals. Violators wait out a willow cooldown equal to three times their burst length. An attacker paying for N identities must also pay for N staggered warm-up schedules, roughly N× minutes of idle traffic, making mass admission slow and observable.
